title: Reading Pattern Abbreviations
description: Learn the shorthand that patterns use so written instructions stop feeling like code.

content.summary: Pattern abbreviations compress stitch names, actions, and repeats into a compact line you can scan quickly.
content.whyItMatters: If you can decode abbreviations, you can follow more patterns, compare designers, and move faster through instructions.
steps: Learn the core stitch abbreviations first: ch, sc, hdc, dc, tr, sl st.
Watch for action words like inc, dec, rep, and sk.
Check whether the designer is using US or UK terms before you start.
Read one full line slowly and expand each abbreviation into plain language.
Mark repeats and counts before crocheting the row.
content.practice: Take one short pattern line and rewrite it in full words before working it.
commonMistakes: Mixing UK and US terms in the same project.
Missing repeat brackets or parentheses while reading quickly.
